title: 24.6 A Power- and Area-Efficient 4nm Self-Calibrated 12b/16GS/s Hierarchical Time-Interleaving ADC
problem: Array processing systems (wideband comms, phased-array radar) require multiple high-speed, low-power ADCs on-chip; thermal and area constraints demand extreme power/area efficiency per channel while maintaining high-speed sampling (16 GS/s) and resolution (12-bit).
motivation: Advanced wireless (5G/6G) and sensing systems need multiple parallel ADC channels at fine lithography (4nm); power and area per converter dominate power budget in RF front-end SoCs.
method: Hierarchical time-interleaving architecture with self-calibration reduces mismatch errors across interleaved stages. 4nm FinFET integration yields compact layout; on-chip reference buffers and supply regulation minimize external component count. Progressive sampling and digital calibration suppress channel mismatches.
key_novelty: Hierarchical interleaving with integrated self-calibration achieved high SNDR (70+ dB) and narrow spurs (<-68 dBFS) at 16 GS/s in 4nm without external trim/tuning.
contributions: 12-bit/16GS/s ADC in 0.43 mm² (4nm), 570 mW including calibration and regulation
Schreier FoM of 148 dB at Nyquist; 172 dB area-normalized FoM
Self-calibrated hierarchical interleaving suppresses mismatch spurs below -68 dBc
High-frequency SFDR >58 dBc with -1 dBFS tone at 7.4 GHz

metrics.other: SNDR 70 dB, Schreier FoM 148 dB, SFDR 58 dBc

limitations: Limited discussion of power breakdown or yield/process variation impact across corners.
primary_theme: Hierarchical time-interleaved ADC for wireless multi-channel RF
